frase_gancho.texto: Long before it was a castle, this hill already served as a place to observe the sun, live beside the lakes, and watch over the valley.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: The tour begins on a hill, not in a building. An INAH bulletin on the archaeological research at Chapultepec describes the hill as a volcanic cone. It formed between twenty-three and five million years ago and came to lie beside the lakes of the valley. The same text says that settled groups used the hill to observe the sun and keep track of time. It also states that the area was inhabited for at least two thousand years, and that the Teotihuacán, the Toltec, and the Mexica occupied it. Since the viceregal period, moreover, the hill was a strategic point for military campaigns. A museum label places its summit about forty-five meters above the level of Mexico City. The castle that crowns it today began to be built in seventeen eighty-five. It was ordered by the viceroy Bernardo de Gálvez, as a place of rest. In this first area you will move from landscape to building, and from a very ancient history to a more recent one.
